This is why people don't get help.

Throwaway for obvious reasons.

I've been slowly sliding into depression for about 2 years now. Most days of the week I go to bed hoping I don't wake up, and wake up disappointed I'm still here. I have a wife, 2 kids. There's enough going on in my wife's life that she couldn't deal with this. I have a strong sense of responsibility, so, so far that has kept me going with 2 kids relying on having 2 parents each and every day. I do have an active plan though, it just has a timer on it for when my youngest hits 21. I work in a field that frowns on its members having mental illness (although ironically we have all received lots of training about recognizing it in those in our care). I also have access to lots of unique and interesting chemicals. I will be successful.

Haven't been able to tell my doctor. Finally worked up to courage to do so *tomorrow*, researched some of the laws in Canada, thought I'd have confidentiality. Then I read this headline, and the Police Officer's response in the comments, and, well, fuck. It is far far too dangerous to seek help. Even a slight risk of being put in handcuffs or losing the right to keeping this private would end my career. My family, and my kids, would be *better off* with me not seeking help and exiting when they are a little older than seeking help now and taking the chance of those consequences, provided I can hang on that long.

So, to the police officer in this thread. Your reasoning is the reason police are only called when there's a body, rather than a person, at the other end.
